_readme: Every variable this chain needs from OUTSIDE itself, and the source the owner's machine resolves it from. A parity run (CM-2) fills the values by running HIS resolution over these source strings for the brand under test, then passes the result as --config. It is a TEMPLATE, not a config: it names no brand and holds no value (workspace rule 7, rule-9 (brand home)), and the engine never reads it. Brand-shaped values are files under brands/<brand>/ — the chain declares that home as the root `brand_home` and the run supplies the read text; nothing brand-substituted is stored in this chain.

today.means: computed by his machine at run time

source.means: supplied by the run — the teardown record, or raw copy to swipe. His positional argument, read through his multi-shape path probe

formats.means: rendered from his bank by machine/formats.py against the brand root; data, not a hand-kept table, which is why the bank was not resolved into this chain

avatars.means: a query against the brand's language banks — the avatar roster line his runner builds, or the no-banks sentinel

concept_brief.means: his triage and spec outputs joined; a derived value here only because inputs bind one reference per name — see provenance.gaps

context_index.means: the index of everything the brand knows, built by his machine/context.py

always_loaded.means: the files loaded regardless of what the scout picks — the product file and the brand's avatar, language and offer banks

avatar.means: a brand-home file, read by his machine AFTER triage names the avatar; his brand map (variables/copy.md) may redirect it

language_bank.means: a brand-home file, read by his machine; his brand map may redirect it

product_file.means: a brand-home file, named by the run

offer_file.means: a brand-home file, read by his machine; his brand map may redirect it

brand_context.means: the brand files the scout picked, loaded and concatenated by his machine

language_injection.means: the language layer queried for the `injection` entry of language-profile.json

language_hooks.means: the language layer queried for the `hooks` entry of language-profile.json

language_expansion.means: the language layer queried for the `expansion` entry of language-profile.json

language_close.means: the language layer queried for the `close` entry of language-profile.json

language_render.means: the language layer queried for the `render` entry of language-profile.json

hook_count.means: supplied when the run started; his default is 5

output_formats.means: supplied when the run started; his default is every format in the bank — what we are WRITING, not what the source was

channel.means: supplied when the run started; where the copy runs

source_reference.means: supplied by the run — the link or name of the source, for the brief; his default is the source filename stem

brand_home.means: the one brand home (rule-9). The chain declares it; a run points it elsewhere with --root brand_home=PATH, which the same check judges
